correctness.rationale: Exact three-projector decomposition yields the heat kernel and its square for all star sizes, and the Nyström trace-gain difference factors as a strictly positive prefactor times the negative of a strictly decreasing exponential sum. The root is unique; stationary-eigenvector leverage probabilities, diagonal probabilities and fixed-time limits are exact. The Lambert scale follows from the exact threshold equation with z=m t of logarithmic size. The bundled checker passed 15458 rational/numeric assertions; these illustrate rather than replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Full or substantial primary-text inspection establishes that Gittens–Mahoney 2013 and Drineas–Mahoney 2005 supply general Nyström sampling and matrix-error frameworks; Chen–Epperly–Tropp–Webber 2024 treats general Cholesky pivot strategies and trace residuals, without giving the unweighted-star heat-kernel crossing. The exact unique scalar heat-time transition and its Lambert-scale heuristic failures are not identified in queried published research records. A prior screened-star resolvent classification uses a different spectral function and gives a size-independent single-pivot transition, rather than the present heat time that vanishes with size. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof that no equivalent theorem exists.
residual_risks: A pre-existing exact heat-star Nyström optimization may be absent from indexed title/semantic search; publication-priority verification remains necessary.

Single-column facts follow fairly directly from a three-eigenvalue spectral decomposition; their research value rests on the motivated sharp crossover and surprising large-star sampling failure, not on a novel general matrix inequality.
Historical screened-resolvent star analogues share the same first-pivot objective, but not the heat-time threshold or Lambert asymptotics; further equivalence checks could alter originality.

value.rationale: A naturally motivated one-landmark compression objective on a standard graph diffusion kernel has a unique and quantitatively sharp optimal landmark migration. The conventional largest-diagonal heuristic always picks a leaf even when the hub is uniquely optimal; for fixed t and large m, both rank-one leverage and diagonal-proportional first-pivot sampling choose that optimal hub with probability tending to zero, with a nonvanishing absolute expected trace regret \(1-e^{-t}\). This supplies an exact benchmark and a meaningful failure mode for first-pivot design; no relative-regret or multipivot guarantee is claimed.
